provenance.disputed_measurement: UNRESOLVED, and this refresh is the third data point. M4 PR 8a review MIN-3 measured every row 90-94% lower than the 2026-07-25/26 numbers (die full 985.9 ms vs ~14-17 s) and blamed contention; those two refreshes reproduced each other within +/-20% and blamed a differently-optimised build. The M5 PR 12 refresh below lands on MIN-3's side (die full 1103.5 ms, i.e. -98% against the superseded 51661.1 ms) on a verified-quiet machine, which rules contention OUT as the explanation for the gap and leaves a build/environment difference (RUSTFLAGS / CARGO_PROFILE_* / target dir / toolchain) as the standing hypothesis - untested, because nobody has yet captured the two environments side by side. Treat cross-refresh comparisons of the absolute numbers as meaningless until someone does; see 'portability'.
provenance.epsilon: CAD_TOLERANCE_EPS unset (the bootstrap default) - the row is ambient-eps agnostic by design.
provenance.load_conditions: Measured with ZERO other cargo build/test lanes running (verified immediately before the run: zero cargo/rustc processes, 1-minute load average 0.82, a parallel agent lane's release build having just drained), RUSTFLAGS unset, no CARGO_PROFILE_* overrides; the only rustflag in effect is the committed x86-64-v3 CPU floor in .cargo/config.toml. A SECOND refresh attempted 25 minutes later, with another lane active, read 20-30x HIGHER on every row (die full 26641.5 ms) and was DISCARDED - a live demonstration that this file means nothing unless the zero-lane check passes, and the reason 'refreshed_under' now records the load average as well as the process count.
provenance.machine: developer workstation (WSL2, 8 cores, ~9 GB RAM) shared with other agent build lanes.
provenance.method: median of 3 runs in one process, std::time::Instant, sequential evaluation schedule (EvalOptions::default()).
provenance.portability: BOX-RELATIVE. Absolute milliseconds do not transfer between machines or load states; only the SHAPE is the signal (relative cost per document, and the full-vs-incremental ratio). Expect large +/-% on the first hosted-CI run and re-refresh from CI when hosted Actions returns.
provenance.profile: cargo test dev profile: opt-level 0 for the kernel crates, opt-level 2 only for spade and mesh (root Cargo.toml). NOT release-representative.
provenance.refreshed_by: M6-5 (ev/m6-5-selection), 2026-08-06 - the corpus gained die_composed, so ONE row was grafted and NOTHING was re-timed. A full refresh was run and DISCARDED: every pre-existing row read 20-25x higher than the committed values (die_fillet full 1001.4 ms vs 25.9 ms), the exact signature 'load_conditions' says means a contended machine (1-minute load 2.85, a parallel review lane active). The die_composed numbers below were measured in that same contended run and are therefore NOT comparable with the rows around them - they exist so the coverage row has its key, not as a datum. Re-refresh the WHOLE file from a verified-quiet machine or hosted CI before reading any cross-row comparison that involves die_composed. M5 PR 12 fix pass F5 (ev/m5-pr12-fillets), 2026-08-03 - the corpus gained die_pips, so every row was re-measured in one run rather than one row being grafted onto a 2026-07-26 file. ALL ELEVEN pre-existing rows moved by -92% to -98%; that is an environment shift, not a speedup this PR earned - see 'disputed_measurement'. The `documents` block is exactly that run's table, with one hand edit and no re-timing: the run also emitted a `die_fillet` row, and that document was pulled back out of the registry afterwards (it refuses at the Interval scalar - see corpus/die_fillet.rs), so its row was DELETED rather than left behind as a stale key.
provenance.status: REPORTING ONLY - measured, never gated (M4-PLAN F8; PERF-PLAN stays advisory). No CI row fails on these numbers.
